head: a142503dc1a6f85b498a425aa58d6a78136ccc6b
head_publication: local only at authoring; pinned GitHub links may not resolve until publication
scope: git diff merge-base..local HEAD; all eleven engine/test/build/script files
method: Known-symbol extraction with lexical brace/parenthesis matching, followed by manual diff-hunk ownership audit; source ranges include forward declarations and definitions separately. A relocated struct has separate deleted/added file occurrences.

files.file_level_explanation: Migrates the existing server loader’s individual insertion options to the force bitmask.
Replaces attrinfo-only sizing/selection with an adapter; removes two private helpers and relocates the plan struct.
Adds representation-based shared sizing/selection and byte-preserving workspace demotion; object_domain.h supports fixed-domain disk sizing and algorithm supports candidate sorting/min/max.
Exports the shared metadata/size plan and the two storage entry points with output ownership documented.
Adds heap_oos.hpp for the new storage call, the SA-only adapter, workspace provenance plumbing and force-flag call migrations.
Defines force option bits and changes the public insertion signature/default, retaining GNU-indent guards around C++ defaults.

Registers and builds the utility-level GoogleTest target test_oos_workspace in the established SA_MODE test list. The executable links cubridsa/GTest and uses existing compile definitions/includes. A new CTest entry is RUN_SERIAL with TIMEOUT 240; each GoogleTest case owns its private database/registry instead of unittestdb. No function, struct, or CMake function/macro definition is added or changed.

Adds a manual Release benchmark outside CTest: INSTALL OUTPUT LABEL [REPEATS], three repeats by default, with 100,000 rows of 48-byte payloads and 10,000 rows of 5,000-byte payloads. Each sample has a private database/configuration, uses real loaddb -S, records elapsed/user/system CPU CSV through /usr/bin/time, verifies values/row bounds, saves SHOW HEAP OOS output, deletes successful sample databases, and retains inputs/outputs/measurements. mkdir requires a new output directory. There are no shell function definitions; the loops and awk programs are top-level script logic. The final local commit corrects its license template. Merely adding the script establishes no measured performance claim.

Adds test_oos_sql_workspace_bytes to the registered SQL CTest entries and to the shared OOS_DB fixture-required, RUN_SERIAL, TIMEOUT 30 property group. The existing SQL source glob/target loop handles its build. No function, struct, or CMake function/macro definition is added or changed.
Adds in-process byte/selection comparison coverage; existing SQL environment plus heap/workspace/primitive APIs provide independent writers and scope_exit provides decoded-collection cleanup.
Adds real standalone utility coverage; filesystem/POSIX process headers support isolated execution and exact LOB evidence, and namespace fs aliases std::filesystem locally.

symbols.what: The old private sizing helper computed each fixed or variable DB_VALUE column’s serialized size and returned their sum.
symbols.why_exists: The old attrinfo-only OOS planner needed a payload total and a size for each demotion candidate.
symbols.why_changed: Its DB_VALUE sizing work is now performed while filling heap_oos_column_plan in heap_attrinfo_determine_disk_layout; the shared planner sums those sizes. Removing this helper removes the dependency of selection policy on HEAP_CACHE_ATTRINFO. Both its forward declaration and body disappear.

symbols.what: The old private helper selected one-, two-, or four-byte variable-offset entries and counted the record header, VOT, and fixed-attribute bound bitmap.
symbols.why_exists: Demotion decisions need the whole inline record size, and moving values out of row can narrow the VOT.
symbols.why_changed: Its representation-based calculation moves to heap_oos_record_header_size in heap_oos.cpp, which accepts OR_CLASSREP and a payload size rather than an attrinfo object. Its declaration and definition are removed so both writers use one calculation.

symbols.what: The former file-local plan held selection, the resulting head OOS OID, full serialized length, and chain identity stamp for one attribute.
symbols.why_exists: The heap writer needs to connect the planner’s decision with the OOS insert result and the later inline stub.
symbols.why_changed: The type is relocated and extended in heap_oos.hpp. This deletion is a move, not removal of the concept: shared selection also needs the attribute metadata and already-known serialized disk size.

symbols.what: The adapter from a heap attribute cache to the shared OOS plan. Its existing pointer-output signature and private declaration remain.
symbols.why_exists: SQL/query-executor and other DB_VALUE writers still start from HEAP_CACHE_ATTRINFO rather than a serialized workspace record.
symbols.why_changed: It now fills each plan entry with last_attrepr plus tp_domain_disk_size for fixed attributes or pr_data_writeval_disk_size for variable values, then delegates to heap_oos_determine_disk_layout. The previous forced-selection, candidate sorting, gate, and offset-width calculation leave this function. This deliberately makes policy shared while preserving the existing DB_VALUE writer entry point.

symbols.what: Shared per-attribute state: attribute points to OR_ATTRIBUTE; disk_size is the existing serialized size; selected marks demotion; oid, length, and identity_stamp describe the newly inserted OOS value chain.
symbols.why_exists: One plan must work for values measured through DB_VALUE and values measured from VOT spans without requiring either representation to be decoded.
symbols.why_changed: The file-local struct moves here and gains attribute=nullptr and disk_size=0. Existing defaults remain selected=false, OID_INITIALIZER, length=0, NULL_LSA. Callers supply all metadata and sizes before invoking the planner; returned OIDs and stamps are subsequently used to write the 24-byte stub.

symbols.what: The public declaration for metadata-and-size-based OOS selection; parameters expose representation, MVCC class state, a mutable plan, and references for offset width, inline size, and has_oos.
symbols.why_exists: The DB_VALUE adapter in heap_file.c and workspace demoter in heap_oos.cpp need one policy boundary.
symbols.why_changed: It makes the extracted planner callable across translation units. There are no default parameters; input metadata and sizes must already be populated. Its definition and detailed policy are covered under heap_oos.cpp.

symbols.what: The public storage entry point for applying OOS Demotion to an already serialized, current-representation workspace record.
symbols.why_exists: Locator force needs storage-layer work without owning the binary-layout implementation.
symbols.why_changed: The contract states that source bytes stay unchanged, result->data remains NULL when unchanged, and a new successful buffer belongs to the caller and must be freed with db_private_free. OOS writes belong to the caller’s existing force top operation. Its definition is covered under heap_oos.cpp.

symbols.what: A private representation-based replacement for the deleted attrinfo header-size helper. It counts the MVCC/non-MVCC insert header, fixed bound bits, and VOT at the smallest fitting offset width.
symbols.why_exists: Both writers must predict the same inline layout after demotion, including VOT width transitions.
symbols.why_changed: It removes the need for HEAP_CACHE_ATTRINFO, uses size_t for payload/header accounting, starts at OR_BYTE_SIZE, widens past OR_MAX_BYTE and OR_MAX_SHORT, and returns the header size. The planner recalculates after forced demotion and after the largest-first loop; the loop itself retains its initial header estimate to preserve base policy.

symbols.what: The shared selection policy over OR_CLASSREP and a vector of serialized column sizes. It returns selected entries, offset width, compact inline size, and whether any OOS value is selected.
symbols.why_exists: A workspace record already contains serialized values, so selection should use metadata and byte lengths without creating DB_VALUE objects or duplicating SQL policy.
symbols.why_changed: It extracts the policy from heap_file.c: clear selection, sum payload, apply FORCE_OUTLINE only to variable values strictly larger than OR_OOS_INLINE_SIZE, then if the record plus MVCC growth exceeds the existing DB_PAGESIZE/4 gate, sort remaining candidates by ordinary-before-PREFER_INLINE, largest size first, then descending plan index. Demote until the conservative estimate fits or candidates run out, recompute the header, and translate candidate-vector bad_alloc into ER_OUT_OF_VIRTUAL_MEMORY. NULL values naturally fail the size floor; the DB_VALUE-specific null test is no longer needed.

symbols.what: The private byte-level implementation that validates a workspace RECDES, plans OOS Demotion, writes selected byte spans, and builds a fresh compact heap record.
symbols.why_exists: Workspace serialization has already assigned references, copied LOB locators, and advanced CHN. Decoding and re-encoding every value adds cost and risks repeating side effects or changing a valid encoding.
symbols.why_changed: It measures variable values from adjacent VOT offsets, supplies fixed sizes from domains, and maps attribute array indices to variable locations. It keeps a small ordinary record unchanged before allocating per-row arrays; FORCE_OUTLINE bypasses this shortcut. If selected, it rejects OOS+REC_BIGONE before writes, resets publication, batches original byte spans through heap_oos_insert_serialized_values, copies fixed/bound bytes and unselected spans exactly, writes 24-byte OOS inline stubs, rewrites VOT/flags, preserves CHN, and reserves MVCC growth room. It never frees source storage or begins a new transaction boundary.

symbols.what: The exported guard and lifetime wrapper around the private demoter.
symbols.why_exists: Locator needs a CUBRID error-return boundary around representation-cache acquisition and potentially throwing vector operations.
symbols.why_changed: It requires an empty result buffer, skips root-class metadata and records already marked HAS_OOS, acquires the current class representation, invokes the private helper, translates bad_alloc, always returns the representation to the cache, and frees any allocated result on error. On success, a NULL result means reuse source; a non-NULL result remains caller-owned. Transaction rollback, rather than this memory cleanup, undoes OOS writes.

symbols.what: A named set of independent insert-force behavior bits, combined into the int force_flags parameter.
symbols.why_exists: Insert force already had three independent boolean options; workspace provenance adds a fourth choice that must compose with bulk and foreign-key behavior.
symbols.why_changed: It replaces the trailing positional booleans with explicit bit combinations and introduces FROM_WORKSPACE. This is a source-level API change in server/SA code; both public declaration and every affected caller in the diff are covered below.

symbols.what: No optional insert-force behavior.
symbols.why_exists: A zero value is needed for ordinary callers and conditional bit expressions.
symbols.why_changed: The new default parameter uses it, preserving the former false/false/false combinations.

symbols.what: The transaction holds a BU_LOCK for bulk insertion.
symbols.why_exists: Heap force distinguishes bulk operations when choosing locking/insertion behavior.
symbols.why_changed: It encodes the former has_BU_lock boolean; loader and multi-insert callers preserve their lock-derived value.

symbols.what: Skip foreign-key rechecking at force time.
symbols.why_exists: Some callers already validate foreign keys before force.
symbols.why_changed: It replaces the former dont_check_fk boolean; server loaddb retains its explicit skip and multi-insert preserves its argument.

symbols.what: Use page-granularity bulk logging for the insert.
symbols.why_exists: The multi-insert optimization supplies a page watcher and a different logging mode.
symbols.why_changed: It replaces use_bulk_logging; only the existing bulk page insertion branch adds this bit.

symbols.what: The RECDES came from workspace serialization and still needs force-time OOS Demotion.
symbols.why_exists: Heap/query and replication writers must be distinguishable from the omitted SA workspace route.
symbols.why_changed: xlocator_force sets it for workspace INSERT, and partition moves propagate it to destination INSERT. The helper gates actual demotion on SA_MODE; merely setting this bit on SERVER_MODE does not run the new demoter.

symbols.what: The public declaration of the heap-and-index insert primitive.
symbols.why_exists: Loader, locator, query-force and replication paths share the same insertion mechanism.
symbols.why_changed: The trailing has_BU_lock, dont_check_fk, use_bulk_logging=false parameters become int force_flags=LC_FORCE_FLAG_NONE. This default supplies the former all-false behavior for callers that omit it. The C++ declaration is wrapped with INDENT-OFF/ON so GNU indent preserves the default parameter.

symbols.what: A private locator adapter that may redirect its local RECDES pointer to a newly demoted buffer.
symbols.why_exists: Insert and update force need the same SA-only storage call and a simple unchanged-record result.
symbols.why_changed: In SA_MODE it invokes heap_oos_demote_workspace_record and redirects *recdes_p only on success with non-NULL output data. In SERVER_MODE it returns NO_ERROR without storage work. The caller retains workspace_recdes for cleanup; the source copyarea is never replaced or freed here.

symbols.what: The primitive that chooses the insertion heap, creates a heap operation context, writes the object, and maintains indexes and related force state.
symbols.why_exists: Multiple higher-level writers need one place to enforce heap, partition and index insertion semantics.
symbols.why_changed: It decodes force_flags into the former three booleans plus from_workspace, adds an empty workspace_recdes, and invokes the SA demoter after partition_prune_insert has selected real_class_oid/real_hfid and before heap_create_insert_context. This ensures OOS chains belong to the destination heap. It frees the optional output at shared error2 cleanup on success or failure. Existing query/replication callers use zero flags and avoid new demotion.

symbols.what: The private primitive for updating a forced object, including reserved-OID writes, instance indexes, class metadata, and possible partition movement.
symbols.why_exists: A workspace flush may represent a logically new row as UPDATE because a forward reference has already reserved its permanent OID; row triggers also route SQL updates through workspace.
symbols.why_changed: Its private declaration gains bool from_workspace=false, preserving all unchanged callers; the definition takes the explicit final boolean. It allocates workspace_recdes, passes provenance through locator_move_record when pruning selects another child, and for an in-heap instance update demotes after pruning and before index/heap writes. Cleanup frees the optional buffer. Root-class metadata is excluded by the heap wrapper. An INSERT-only fix would miss both reserved OIDs and workspace UPDATE.

symbols.what: The private UPDATE helper that inserts a row into the selected child partition and deletes it from its previous heap.
symbols.why_exists: Changing a partition key may change the destination heap, requiring insertion and deletion rather than an in-place update.
symbols.why_changed: Both private declaration and definition gain a required final from_workspace boolean. Both destination insertion variants translate it to FROM_WORKSPACE or NONE, so demotion occurs in destination INSERT after ownership has been selected. It does not demote in the old child or introduce chain sharing between heaps.

symbols.what: The copyarea handler for batches of instance UPDATE operations performed through the client/workspace path.
symbols.why_exists: Multi-row workspace updates have shared unique-statistics and force bookkeeping distinct from single-row flushes.
symbols.why_changed: It adds an explicit true as locator_update_force’s final from_workspace argument. The already-existing need_locking=true remains the preceding boolean. This covers trigger-selected multi-row workspace UPDATE in SA; the SA_MODE adapter remains the effective mode gate.

symbols.what: The normal workspace copyarea dispatcher for INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE, owning an outer force top operation and optional per-object top operations.
symbols.why_exists: It turns dirty workspace records into persistent heap/index changes and supports ignored object errors.
symbols.why_changed: INSERT variants now pass FROM_WORKSPACE; UPDATE variants pass from_workspace=true. DELETE behavior stays as the existing code. New OOS writes therefore execute inside the existing outer top operation and, for filtered errors, the existing per-object rollback boundary. It also delegates multi-row updates to the separately changed handler.

symbols.what: The replication apply copyarea dispatcher, including replica OOS handling and per-object apply errors.
symbols.why_exists: Replication replays already prepared row/OOS state with its own publication and transaction handling.
symbols.why_changed: The insert call drops the former explicit false/false arguments and relies on force_flags=NONE. This is an API migration only: it does not label replica data as workspace-originated or run the new SA demoter. Its transaction and OOS fixup logic is outside the PR’s semantic change.

symbols.what: The force path that starts from HEAP_CACHE_ATTRINFO, transforms DB_VALUEs to a record, then inserts or updates heap/index storage.
symbols.why_exists: SQL/query execution already has DB_VALUE-based serialization and OOS preparation.
symbols.why_changed: Its insertion call omits the former false/false arguments and takes the new default NONE. It intentionally leaves FROM_WORKSPACE unset because its record has already passed the attrinfo writer and shared planner. Its UPDATE call keeps the new private default from_workspace=false.

symbols.what: The existing internal partition-data redistribution routine that fetches rows and inserts them into the partition arrangement.
symbols.why_exists: Partition DDL needs a specialized row-moving path preserving existing MVCC identity and storage semantics.
symbols.why_changed: Its insert call drops false/false and takes force_flags=NONE, preserving UPDATE_INPLACE_OLD_MVCCID. This is a call-signature migration; the PR’s workspace-provenance path is not added to redistribution. Do not confuse this routine with workspace UPDATE’s changed locator_move_record.

symbols.what: The multi-record insert routine used by the server loader, with ordinary fallback and an optimized heap-page insertion branch.
symbols.why_exists: Batch insertion can reduce per-row page and logging overhead while retaining individual-force fallbacks.
symbols.why_changed: It composes force_flags from the actual BU lock and dont_check_fk argument once. Ordinary/fallback calls use those bits; the watcher-assisted bulk-page branch adds BULK_LOGGING. None of these calls sets FROM_WORKSPACE because the server loader already transforms its DB_VALUEs. Its own public signature stays the same.

symbols.what: The cubload server loader method that forces the collected record batch, either individually for filtered errors/HA or through multi-insert.
symbols.why_exists: Client-server loading prepares DB_VALUE-based records before force and needs lock, foreign-key, error-filter, and replication behavior preserved during batching.
symbols.why_changed: It creates force_flags=DONT_CHECK_FK plus HAS_BU_LOCK when held, and passes this bitmask in the individual insertion call. This exactly represents the previous has_BU_lock,true,false arguments. It is an API migration caused by locator_insert_force’s change; it does not add SA workspace demotion to this already-prepared server loader path.

symbols.what: The GoogleTest fixture for actual installed cubrid/csql utilities; each case owns a private temporary database, registry, configuration, command logs, deterministic payload, and sequence counter.
symbols.why_exists: In-process db_execute tests alone cannot prove the standalone object-file loader took its real workspace route, and no-logging state must not contaminate another case.
symbols.why_changed: It adds isolated utility-level coverage of loader/workspace storage ownership and errors. root owns evidence; payload is deterministic 5,000-byte VARBIT data; sequence gives unique command filenames; created guards successful cleanup. Failed cases retain their directory and database for investigation.

symbols.what: Reads an evidence file as binary into a string and records an expectation if opening fails.
symbols.why_exists: Command output and LOB bytes must be inspectable without text normalization.
symbols.why_changed: It gives the new fixture a common reader for utility evidence and exact LOB snapshots.

symbols.what: Writes generated SQL, object files, or configuration and asserts successful close.
symbols.why_exists: Utility tests need literal fixtures and useful failure locations.
symbols.why_changed: It creates inputs under the private fixture directory; callers use ASSERT_NO_FATAL_FAILURE where continuation would be invalid.

symbols.what: Executes an argv vector through fork/execvp, pipes a saved input file to stdin, captures stdout/stderr, and validates termination/output.
symbols.why_exists: The fixture must call real utilities while controlling environment, timeouts, and expected rejection.
symbols.why_changed: The child alone sets its registry/configuration and LC_ALL=C, changes directory, and arms a 60-second alarm; the parent handles EINTR and waits. Defaults input="" and expected_error="" mean empty stdin and successful command. A nonempty expected_error requires nonzero exit plus a case-insensitive diagnostic match. Paths/SQL are never shell-interpolated.

symbols.what: Runs csql in standalone mode as DBA with explicit transactions and line output.
symbols.why_exists: Readable SQL assertions must go through the installed SA utility against the private database.
symbols.why_changed: It wraps run with -S, --no-auto-commit, and --line-output for the new utility fixture.

symbols.what: Writes a loaddb object file and runs cubrid loaddb -S with optional arguments and an expected-error expression.
symbols.why_exists: A SQL INSERT would not establish standalone object-file loader coverage.
symbols.why_changed: Default options={} and expected_error="" select ordinary successful loading; callers can request --no-logging or an error-control file and expected rejection. The case’s generated object file is retained with evidence if failure occurs.

symbols.what: Extracts every Oos_num_recs field from SHOW HEAP OOS output and compares the ordered list of counts.
symbols.why_exists: Logical value equality alone cannot prove OOS-path execution or detect orphan chunks.
symbols.why_changed: It checks explicit physical chunk-count observations, including before/after rollback sequences and partition ownership.

symbols.what: Queries a value/row-count predicate and SHOW HEAP OOS, requiring VALUE_OK and an exact chunk count.
symbols.why_exists: Each scenario needs both a logical oracle and independent OOS-path evidence.
symbols.why_changed: It packages these two assertions; rows is the expected count and chunks counts physical chunk records, not logical value chains. Empty-table rejection uses an explicit zero-row query instead of this SUM-based helper.

symbols.what: Creates a primary-key table, chooses insert_execution_mode=0, inserts and commits a large VARBIT row, then verifies one OOS chunk.
symbols.why_exists: Later rollback/error tests need a known committed workspace-produced baseline.
symbols.why_changed: It also exercises reserved-OID handling through a direct workspace INSERT rather than the default query executor.

symbols.what: Creates an object-reference table and loads two mutually referring rows using forward/backward object-file references.
symbols.why_exists: OID reservation can change a pending flush from INSERT to UPDATE.
symbols.why_changed: It proves permanent references and OOS values coexist before tests perform workspace updates and cleanup.

symbols.what: Creates a two-child range-partitioned table and loads one large row into each child.
symbols.why_exists: OOS writes must follow the destination heap rather than the input partitioned root.
symbols.why_changed: It requires one chunk per child, correct row values, and zero chunks owned by the partitioned root.

symbols.what: Snapshots the paths and binary contents of all regular files under the fixture’s external LOB directory.
symbols.why_exists: A value query alone would miss duplicated, replaced, or modified external LOB files.
symbols.why_changed: It provides an exact before/after filesystem oracle for workspace updates that demote another attribute.

symbols.what: Creates a unique directory, isolated configuration, deterministic random VARBIT payload, LOB directory, and fresh 16KB-page database.
symbols.why_exists: Each utility test must begin with independent persistent and no-logging state.
symbols.why_changed: It uses 32MB initial data/log volumes and marks created only after successful setup; generated data avoids string-compression ambiguity.

symbols.what: Deletes a successfully tested private database and directory; failed cases retain their evidence path.
symbols.why_exists: Isolation needs cleanup, but a failing utility scenario needs its inputs, outputs, and database preserved.
symbols.why_changed: It handles partial setup with root/created guards, runs deletedb only for a successful case, and prints the retained path after failure.

symbols.what: A one-row real SA loaddb scenario.
symbols.why_exists: The reported defect is missing OOS Demotion in the standalone object loader.
symbols.why_changed: It requires exact loaded VARBIT value and one physical OOS chunk, catching a successful but fully inline load.

symbols.what: A paired OOS+large-fixed record rejection and ordinary fixed-only REC_BIGONE acceptance scenario.
symbols.why_exists: The demoter must reject unsupported coexistence without banning ordinary overflow records.
symbols.why_changed: It requires the first load to fail with a maximum-record diagnostic, leave zero rows/chunks, and the fixed-only load to succeed with correct value and zero OOS chunks.

symbols.what: A direct workspace INSERT through seed_workspace.
symbols.why_exists: An existing permanent/reserved OID may send a logically new object through update force.
symbols.why_changed: It adds a named regression requiring the row and OOS chain to be stored through the common workspace force route.

symbols.what: Two mutually referencing loaddb rows.
symbols.why_exists: Demotion must preserve previously fixed permanent object references and handle reserved-OID UPDATE.
symbols.why_changed: It checks peer.id relationships, both large values, and exactly two OOS chunks.

symbols.what: Loads through a partitioned root and examines both children and root.
symbols.why_exists: The destination heap is the OOS owner.
symbols.why_changed: It requires child-owned storage and a root count of zero through seed_partitions.

symbols.what: Flushes an uncommitted workspace INSERT using SELECT, observes storage, then rolls back.
symbols.why_exists: A row that merely stayed pending in workspace would not test OOS rollback.
symbols.why_changed: It requires chunk counts 2 then 1 and preservation of the committed seed row/value.

symbols.what: Forces a two-row workspace UPDATE with a row trigger, then separately tests rollback, committed replacement, and DELETE.
symbols.why_exists: Both multi-update provenance and existing SA eager cleanup must stay inside transaction semantics.
symbols.why_changed: It requires correct old values after rollback, replacement values after commit, stable two-chunk ownership, preserved references, and zero chunks after deletion.

symbols.what: Loads a new row followed by a duplicate primary key without an ignored-error rule.
symbols.why_exists: A failing batch must undo previously inserted row/OOS state.
symbols.why_changed: It expects a unique diagnostic and only the committed seed row and its one chunk afterward.

symbols.what: Ignores ER_BTREE_UNIQUE_FAILED (-670), rejects a duplicate row, then loads a valid later row.
symbols.why_exists: The per-object top operation must undo only the failed row’s OOS work and allow continued loading.
symbols.why_changed: It requires both valid IDs, correct values, and two chunks rather than an orphan from the rejected duplicate.

symbols.what: Exercises NULL/empty/small values, a small FORCE_OUTLINE value, unequal largest-first candidates, and a 50,000-byte multichunk value.
symbols.why_exists: The new workspace route must use the same selection policy and storage behavior as DB_VALUE writers.
symbols.why_changed: It requires no OOS for the tiny table, one forced chunk, one largest-first chunk whose aggregate serialized size is just over 3,000 bytes, and four chunks for the multichunk case, while checking every logical value. This case does not independently test PREFER_INLINE; the byte fixture does.

symbols.what: Updates a separate VARBIT attribute while permanent BLOB/CLOB locators remain on the row.
symbols.why_exists: OOS Demotion must preserve serialized external locators without recopying external LOB data.
symbols.why_changed: After trigger-selected rollback and commit it compares BLOB/CLOB values plus exact LOB file paths/bytes. It seeds LOBs through query execution because fresh workspace LOB INSERT has a separate pre-existing defect; it does not claim coverage of every locator-demotion combination.

symbols.what: Changes a partition key through a trigger-selected workspace UPDATE.
symbols.why_exists: The FROM_WORKSPACE marker must survive movement to the destination insertion.
symbols.why_changed: It requires zero chunks in the old child and two correct rows/chunks in the destination child, detecting OOS creation in the wrong heap or leaked source ownership.

symbols.what: Runs --no-logging SA loaddb on a fresh private database and reads back the large value.
symbols.why_exists: Successful no-logging bulk loading remains supported under the accepted OOS logging exception.
symbols.why_changed: It requires the correct row and one chunk. It establishes successful storage/readback only; it does not establish crash recovery, failed-load rollback, or identity-stamp uniqueness without logging.

symbols.what: The utility test binary’s GoogleTest entry point.
symbols.why_exists: CTest needs an executable entry point that accepts GoogleTest filtering and reports its exit code.
symbols.why_changed: It initializes GoogleTest and runs this fixture’s cases; database lifetime belongs to each case, so it does not add the shared SQL server environment.

symbols.what: The in-process GoogleTest fixture comparing a tf_mem_to_disk workspace record with the new demotion result, a DB_VALUE-based reference writer, and the query writer’s stored image.
symbols.why_exists: CLI value/chunk counts cannot prove the demoter copied serialized spans exactly or selected the same columns at encoding/VOT boundaries.
symbols.why_changed: It tracks an optional private output RECDES and whether a test sysop is active. All demotion writes stay in that sysop and teardown aborts them; the table and transaction are also cleaned up. It uses the established OOS SQL fixture infrastructure.

symbols.what: Frees the optional demoted buffer, aborts the test sysop when started, aborts the transaction, drops the test table, and commits cleanup.
symbols.why_exists: Reference serialization and actual demotion create OOS chains during each comparison, and ASSERT failures may stop the test early.
symbols.why_changed: The sysop flag and RECDES_INITIALIZER make cleanup safe after partial progress. Freeing memory and aborting persistent OOS writes are deliberately separate operations.

symbols.what: Compares record HAS_OOS, each variable column’s OOS selection, and its payload read either from an inline span or an actual OOS chain.
symbols.why_exists: Different inserted chains have different physical OIDs/stamps; useful equivalence is selection and payload, with exact bytes where serialization should match.
symbols.why_changed: domains supplies schema metadata for collection decoding. Default logical_collections=false requires exact serialized payload bytes for the workspace reference; true only for the independent query-writer comparison decodes set-like values and checks tp_value_compare==DB_EQ. SQL and workspace collection writers may include/omit an optional domain while representing the same value. This final oracle repair is in local a142503dc; selection equality and workspace byte checks remain strict.

symbols.what: The scope_exit cleanup lambda for the two decoded collection DB_VALUEs in compare.
symbols.why_exists: An ASSERT inside collection decoding can return early, and decoded collections may own allocated memory.
symbols.why_changed: It clears both initialized values on every exit from the decoding block. This accompanies the a142503dc logical-collection oracle repair, rather than a production serialization change.

symbols.what: Builds one schema/value scenario, captures the query writer’s stored row, serializes a fetched workspace object, obtains a DB_VALUE reference, and demotes the same workspace source.
symbols.why_exists: A single helper applies the two independent comparisons and source-preservation assertions consistently to many encodings.
symbols.why_changed: Default alter=nullptr selects a current-schema comparison against the stored query image; a supplied ALTER exercises old-disk/current-workspace conversion and omits the incompatible stored-image comparison. It checks exact workspace-reference payloads, optional logical query collections, OOS selection, final width/length, preserved CHN, and unchanged source bytes. It captures actual stored OOS payloads rather than making a second copy of the input.

symbols.what: An ordinary row containing NULL, empty VARCHAR, and empty VARBIT.
symbols.why_exists: Zero-length and unprofitable values must avoid unnecessary OOS work.
symbols.why_changed: It compares unchanged logical/serialized payloads and selection against both writers.

symbols.what: A 3,500-byte PREFER_INLINE candidate with 3,000- and 600-byte ordinary candidates.
symbols.why_exists: The largest value may need to stay inline because the soft policy puts ordinary candidates first.
symbols.why_changed: It requires identical per-column selection and payloads across the shared workspace/DB_VALUE planners and stored query image.

symbols.what: Two equally sized 2,200-byte ordinary candidates.
symbols.why_exists: A stable tie rule avoids writer-dependent selection.
symbols.why_changed: It checks that the descending attribute-index tie behavior remains shared.

symbols.what: A forced 65,536-byte VARBIT next to a tiny value.
symbols.why_exists: The input’s wide VOT can shrink after most bytes move out of row.
symbols.why_changed: It compares compact offset width/length and exact payload bytes after forced demotion.

symbols.what: Forced VARCHAR and JSON values plus a large VARBIT.
symbols.why_exists: Serialized byte length, rather than text length or a fresh type conversion, must drive selection.
symbols.why_changed: It compares compressed-string and JSON payloads as bytes, demonstrating the demoter does not recompress or reserialize them.

symbols.what: A forced SEQUENCE OF INTEGER plus a large VARBIT.
symbols.why_exists: Collections have multiple valid serialized forms, while the demoter must retain the workspace form exactly.
symbols.why_changed: The workspace-reference comparison remains byte-exact; the independent query comparison uses the final repaired logical collection oracle. Different optional domain bytes alone no longer fail the test.

symbols.what: One forced large VARBIT and seventy additional variable columns alternating NULL and tiny values.
symbols.why_exists: Many VOT entries affect alignment and offset width independently of the largest payload.
symbols.why_changed: It checks attribute-location mapping, fixed/header accounting, null spans, canonical output layout, and exact source payload preservation.

symbols.what: Reads a row written before an ALTER adds a defaulted attribute, then serializes/demotes its current workspace form.
symbols.why_exists: The new demoter intentionally accepts only current-representation workspace records.
symbols.why_changed: It verifies that existing object fetch/serialization performs schema conversion before demotion; the old stored query image is deliberately not compared against the new schema.

symbols.what: A parameterized fixture inheriting OosWorkspaceBytes and WithParamInterface<int>, with no added methods or fields.
symbols.why_exists: The same byte-preservation oracle should run over multiple profitable-size and encoding/VOT boundaries.
symbols.why_changed: It reuses setup-free comparison and teardown behavior while supplying one payload byte count per runtime case.

symbols.what: The parameterized test body for a forced VARBIT of GetParam() bytes, a 200-byte VARBIT, and a 255-character VARCHAR beside a fixed integer.
symbols.why_exists: Eligibility uses serialized disk size, and length prefixes/VOT sizes change near small and large encoding boundaries.
symbols.why_changed: It calls the same check helper for all thirteen parameters; it does not assume the nominal VARBIT payload length equals its serialized span length.

symbols.what: The registration of thirteen SerializedSizesMatchValueSizes cases with values 20,21,24,25,244,248,252,3800,4040,4060,32760,32768,65536.
symbols.why_exists: A TEST_P declaration is not runnable without concrete instantiations, and boundary coverage needs an explicit finite inventory.
symbols.why_changed: It makes each chosen size a real GoogleTest case. The guide lists the runtime names and size purpose below; 4060 is a tested value, not a claim that this HEAD implements the normative 4060-byte record target.

symbols.what: The byte-comparison binary’s GoogleTest entry point with the existing SqlServerEnv global environment.
symbols.why_exists: The comparison calls engine/client APIs directly and therefore needs the established in-process SQL database initialization.
symbols.why_changed: It initializes GoogleTest, installs SqlServerEnv, and runs the cases; it differs from the utility binary because that binary launches separate processes with private databases.

limitations: The inventory is a manual-audited lexical inventory, not a compiler AST export. Generated GoogleTest implementation symbols are represented by their TEST_F/TEST_P declarations and runtime instances.
The guide explains source intent and review obligations; it is not a new formal standards/spec review and does not assert CI failure attribution.
